request: Three linked capabilities. (1) The epic track gains a roadmap-sync step: at the epic commit it writes an epic heading to project.json -> roadmap.path plus one task row per slice from the sliced spec, in the format the standup parser already reads; each epic-child then flips its own row via existing Phase 10.6. (2) A backlog-retriage capability: Claude reads the open backlog entries, proposes candidate epic groupings with rationale, the human confirms, and the confirmed grouping feeds /triage to start a normal epic run. Absorbed backlog entries are closed and removed at the epic commit, never at proposal time. (3) An ad-hoc roadmap resync step that backfills every epic already on disk (.claude/state/epic/*.json) onto the roadmap, so the five existing epics that predate capability (1) get their heading and slice rows. Ad-hoc, not a workflow phase: idempotent, never duplicates an epic already present, and never blocks a commit.
novelty_evidence: Searched .claude/skills/roadmap-sync/sync.mjs: flipTask, flipTaskInEpic, promoteEpicHeading and auditRoadmap all mutate an existing row; no append/create-epic transform exists. Searched the 55 open backlog keys: none names roadmap-epic creation or backlog retriage. Nearest precedents, both adjacent and neither sufficient: .claude/skills/sprint-planner (propose a batch, human confirms, writes workflow.json tickets[]) and .claude/skills/memory-sync/sweep.mjs --mode stamp-closure (backlog closure driven by source_backlog_keys). No spec chapter commits to either capability.
track_reason: Heavier than tdd-quickfix because the change amends docs/init/seed.md section 18.9 and CLAUDE.md Article IV (which today excludes the epic track from roadmap sync), so it needs a written spec and gate A. Lighter than intake-full because the scout and research evidence is already cited in novelty_evidence.
